source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's San Antonio campus publishes 33 MW of IT capacity across 175,000 square feet, sixth among the nineteen Texas facilities that disclose power, but nothing about how that power is used.

The 33 MW is a published IT capacity figure with no stated rack density or accelerator count. At an assumed 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, it implies roughly 825 racks and about 6,600 accelerator slots at eight per rack. That arithmetic illustrates scale, it does not describe a deployment. The certifications, HIPAA, FISMA, PCI DSS, SOC 2 Type 2, TIA-942 and HITRUST, qualify the campus for regulated enterprise, healthcare and federal workloads. Those are baseline requirements for such customers, not markers of AI specialization.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, but only nineteen publish capacity. The disclosed state total is 475 MW, of which this campus is 6.9% and ranks sixth. That rank reflects who discloses rather than who is largest, since an unpublished facility could exceed it.

The data does not cover grid interconnection, power source, or whether the 33 MW is contracted, allocated or available. It also does not say whether any capacity serves AI training rather than the regulated workloads the certifications point to. The suitability score of 68 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion missing. Without those facts, the campus cannot be placed on either side of the grid constraint that governs AI scaling.
